fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents accurately present a data scientist moving toward MLE work, not an established production MLE. Scheduled notebooks, batch SQL scoring, limited Docker work and course-only PyTorch remain clearly bounded. However, the letter does not directly address the central mismatch in production-MLE seniority or the lack of assistant/RAG experience; a brief level-calibration statement would make the application more realistic.

issues: Contact details are absent by explicit user request and should not be treated as a compliance failure.
Education has no institution or dates; these were not supplied and should not be invented.
The two-page count is within the normal range, but the sparse second page is inefficient.
The skills summary repeats scheduled jobs and dbt Cloud Scheduler, while the opening summary repeats several skills listed immediately below.
The Cloud skills line mixes cloud services, transformation tooling and reporting tools rather than separating their functions.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in a sensible order, with intact words and conventional headings.
Model evaluation and fine-tuning are represented by clear semantic equivalents rather than necessarily exact keyword strings.
Production deployment appears only as the platform team's responsibility, not as the candidate's capability.
The CV does not establish four years of production MLE experience.
Most assistant/LLM and production-MLOps requirements are genuinely unsupported by the candidate material; adding them as skills would be misleading.

issues: The technical project paragraph is dense and largely repeats the CV.
The final paragraph repeats the same list of transferable skills instead of adding a sharper explanation of relevance to support AI.
The letter acknowledges a transition but leaves the four-year production-MLE and assistant/RAG gaps implicit.
The candidate's openness to a more junior MLE level could have been used tactfully without inventing experience.
strengths: Correct company, team and role throughout.
Uses the company's support-automation mission and documented ownership, context-sharing and feedback culture.
Preserves the estimated nature of the food-waste benefit.
Explicitly attributes Cloud Run deployment to the platform team.
Updates the earlier letter's employment framing rather than recycling its outdated present-tense analyst role.

spacing_issues: The CV's ADDITIONAL PROJECT heading is orphaned at the bottom of page 1, while its rule and project content start on page 2.
The CV's last page is only 14.5% filled and contains a single short course project, leaving most of the page empty.
The first CV page is comparatively dense, particularly the skills block and eight-bullet current role.
issues: The orphaned heading and separated section rule make the CV look insufficiently checked before export.
A modest reduction in repetitive summary and skills text could likely avoid the nearly empty second page.
The cover letter is cleanly typeset on one page with comfortable paragraph spacing and a compatible serif style.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “orchestrated as scheduled notebook jobs” is understandable but cumbersome; “run as scheduled notebook jobs” would be more direct.
“forecasting, churn modelling, feature engineering, batch-scoring workflows and automated testing” repeats material already covered in the letter.

notes_facts_used: The DS-to-MLE transition and desire to deepen production-engineering experience.
Forecasting is scheduled-notebook work and churn scoring is batch-based, not a self-deployed model API.
Docker work is limited to the Streamlit application's Dockerfile, with deployment owned by the platform team.
Orchestration uses dbt Cloud Scheduler and scheduled notebooks.
GCP experience is scoped to BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench rather than infrastructure expertise.
pytest testing began in 2025 and has approximately 60% coverage of forecasting feature code.
The candidate delivered Stats for PMs three times.
notes_facts_ignored: Openness to a mid-level or junior-ish MLE title.

parsed.summary: These are accurate, credible transition documents that preserve the distinction between scheduled batch workflows, platform-owned deployment and course-only deep learning. The CV uses nearly all relevant evidence, and the letter is tailored to Quillstone's support mission and documented culture without inventing work preferences. The candidate nevertheless falls substantially short of the advertised production-MLE and assistant/RAG requirements, making screening success unlikely. The clearest avoidable defect is the CV pagination: an orphaned project heading leads to a nearly empty second page.
